notes: All vendor market shares (vendorShare) sum to 100.0% in every year across DRAM (2000-2026), NAND (2000-2026), and HDD (2010-2026).

DRAM consolidation milestones: Infineon memory division spun off as Qimonda in 2006 and filed for insolvency in Jan 2009 (0% from 2010); Elpida (NEC/Hitachi/Mitsubishi DRAM) filed for bankruptcy in Feb 2012 and was acquired by Micron in July 2013 (0% from 2014); CXMT entered commercial production in 2020.

NAND consolidation milestones: Kioxia represents Toshiba Memory (rebranded Oct 2019); WDC represents SanDisk (acquired May 2016); SK hynix includes Solidigm (Intel NAND/SSD business acquired Dec 2021, Intel standalone 0% from 2022); YMTC entered commercial 3D NAND volume in 2020.

Wafer capacities (waferCapacityKwpm) are year-end active 300mm-equivalent wafer starts per month in thousands (kWPM). Pre-2006 200mm lines are converted to 300mm equivalents using a 2.25x area factor. 2023 reflects deep industry utilization cuts (55-70% in NAND and legacy DRAM).

HBM wafer penalty (2023-2026E): HBM3E/HBM4 dies consume ~3x the wafer area per bit of standard DDR5 due to larger die size, TSV overhead, and packaging yield, tightening conventional DRAM bit supply even as total DRAM kWPM reaches record highs.

HDD vendor series (2010-2026E): For 2010-2011, WDC is presented pro-forma including HGST (acquired Mar 2012), Seagate includes Samsung HDD (acquired Dec 2011), and Toshiba includes Fujitsu HDD (acquired 2009/2010) so the three surviving OEMs sum to 100% of industry shipments.

Bit demand (bitDemandEB) is derived from shipped bit supply (bitShipmentsEB) and industry sufficiency ratios reported by TrendForce/Coughlin: demand exceeds shipped supply by 3-10% during acute shortages (e.g., 2011-2012 Thai floods in HDD, 2017-2018 memory supercycle, 2021 pandemic crunch, 2024-2026 AI/HBM/nearline tightness) and falls 6-11% below supply during inventory gluts (2001, 2007-2008, 2011-2012 DRAM, 2019, 2022-2023).
